R0168.title: Rug Pull (Exit Scam)
R0168.definition: Web3 project teams suddenly withdrawing funds and disappearing after raising capital or attracting liquidity, causing investor funds to become worthless.
R0168.description: Rug Pull is a common fraud method in the cryptocurrency space. Project teams attract users to invest or provide liquidity through false promotions, then abscond with funds by removing liquidity pools, transferring contract ownership, or exploiting backdoor functions. Some projects appear legitimate but have pre-embedded code vulnerabilities that harvest users at the opportune moment.
R0168.influence: Complete loss of investor funds, damage to Web3 ecosystem trust, attracts regulatory attention.

references.title: Investor Alert: 5 Ways Fraudsters May Lure Victims Into Scams Involving Crypto Assets - SEC
Crypto Scams: 2021 Rug Pulls Put Revenues Near All-Time High - Chainalysis
Crypto Scam Tracker: Rug Pull Scam - California DFPI

observables: The project's liquidity pool is suddenly removed by the project team after fundraising, with the token price instantly dropping to zero
Backdoor functions pre-embedded in the contract (such as minting, pausing trades, transferring ownership) are invoked at the opportune moment
After the project team runs false high-yield promotions on social media, team addresses transfer funds to a mixer
A new project's contract goes live without audit, with permission fields centrally controlled by a single address
